verdicts.threatModel: A network attacker substituting a downloaded binary is the rule's model; here the flagged text is a rustdoc module comment citing the SQLite file-format specification page, so no download and no attacker-controlled bytes exist.
verdicts.reachability: Line 4 sits inside `//!` doc comments describing the clean-room page reader; the URL is never passed to any HTTP client and is stripped at compile time, so it is unreachable at runtime.
verdicts.impact: None: the SQLite reader parses a local Lightroom catalog the user selects and has no SQLite runtime dependency; the fileformat.html link fetches nothing that could be executed or loaded.
verdicts.rationale: Scanner matched an https URL in documentation; lightroom_sqlite.rs:4 is a `//!` comment referencing sqlite.org/fileformat.html, not a binary download, so no digest is applicable.

verdicts.threatModel: No supply-chain attacker applies: the hit is an RDF namespace IRI inside the `const XMP` test fixture used to exercise preset import mapping.
verdicts.reachability: preset_import.rs:579 opens `#[cfg(test)]`, so the fixture at line 704 compiles only into unit tests; XML namespace IRIs are identifiers, never dereferenced by the XMP parser.
verdicts.impact: None: no file is downloaded or executed; the string is parsed in-process by test assertions on crs:Exposure2012/Vibrance mapping.
verdicts.rationale: w3.org rdf-syntax-ns IRI in a cfg(test) preset fixture is a namespace name, not a binary URL; digest pinning is meaningless for it.

verdicts.threatModel: Considered attacker: someone tampering with the SAM 3 model download. The flagged constant, however, is LICENSE_URL, a GitHub blob page for the model licence shown to the user before downloading.
verdicts.reachability: LICENSE_URL is only displayed as licence text/link (doc comment at line 35: shown before downloading); it is not part of any FileSpec handed to the fetcher. The checkpoint itself is pinned in crates/segment/src/fetch/mod.rs:22-25 with an explicit sha256.
verdicts.impact: None from this line: a licence web page is never downloaded or executed by Ember. (Separately, fetch/mod.rs:20-21 fetch vocab.json/merges.txt tokenizer text with sha256 None, but those are bounded text files, not this candidate.)
verdicts.rationale: segment/mod.rs:37 is a human-facing licence link, not a binary URL; the model weights download carries a sha256 pin at crates/segment/src/fetch/mod.rs:25.

verdicts.threatModel: Considered: an attacker serving altered ONNX weights from a catalog URL. This test catalog points at models.example.org and supplies `sha256` from sha256_file(path) on the next line.
verdicts.reachability: tests_face_models is cfg(test) (lib.rs:1062 region); example.org is a reserved documentation domain. The entry at line 434 carries a sha256 digest and line 435 sizeBytes, so the URL is in fact pinned.
verdicts.impact: None: in production crates/faces/src/catalog.rs:88-89 rejects any catalog entry lacking sha256 or sizeBytes, so a download is always checked against a digest.
verdicts.rationale: The scanner missed the adjacent sha256 at tests_face_models.rs:434; the URL is digest-pinned and test-only.

verdicts.threatModel: Threat considered is user-catalog weight tampering for the `my-research-model` entry; the same JSON object carries `"sha256": sha` computed at line 553.
verdicts.reachability: Test-only module; the sha256 key is on line 556 directly following the URL, so a scanner looking only at line 555 missed it. No real host is contacted (models.example.org).
verdicts.impact: None: the entry is pinned by digest and size; catalog.rs:88-89 enforces this for every real catalog entry.
verdicts.rationale: my-research-model test entry is pinned via sha256 on the next line; the candidate is a line-window artefact of the scanner.

verdicts.threatModel: Considered an unpinned model entry ('No hash'). This is a deliberate negative fixture proving the loader refuses catalog entries without a digest.
verdicts.reachability: Test-only; the `broken` entry has no sha256 on purpose, and crates/faces/src/catalog.rs:88-89 returns 'needs `sha256` and `sizeBytes`' for it, so it is never offered for download.
verdicts.impact: None: the production control this fixture exercises blocks exactly the risk the scanner reports; the entry is listed as an error, not downloaded.
verdicts.rationale: Line 558 is a negative test case for the enforced sha256 requirement (catalog.rs:88-89); it demonstrates the mitigation rather than a vulnerability.
